findings.claim: Removing the `case <= byte.MaxValue` branch from the string-header writer changes the wire format for every string of 32–255 UTF-8 bytes. They are now written as str16 (0xda plus a 2-byte length, 3 bytes) instead of str8 (0xd9 plus a 1-byte length, 2 bytes). Every such string grows by one byte and no longer matches base-built bytes, which breaks byte-for-byte compatibility (hashes, golden files, other MessagePack implementations' canonical output). This is unrelated to REQ-2234 and violates the criterion that behaviour without SuppressSourceGeneration does not change.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.StringHeaderStr8ReceiptTests.StringOf40BytesUsesStr8Header. It calls MessagePackPrimitives.TryWriteStringHeader(buffer, 40, out written) and expects written == 2 and buffer[0] == MessagePackCode.Str8 (0xd9). On head it writes 3 bytes starting with 0xda. Confirm with a byte-diff of MessagePackSerializer.Serialize(new string('a', 40)) built from base and from head.

findings.claim: The new `if (!intMembers.ContainsKey(...))` and `if (!stringMembers.ContainsKey(...))` guards silently drop the second member that shares a key with an earlier one. No diagnostic is reported for it. Before the change the duplicate made the collector throw, which was a loud failure. Now a [MessagePackObject] with two [Key(0)] members gets no analyzer error, and the generated formatter omits the second member, so its data is silently never serialized. The dynamic resolver used under SuppressSourceGeneration = true rejects duplicate keys at run time, yet the analyzer stays silent, which runs against the requirement that the analyzer report violations.

It runs all MessagePack analyzers over a public [MessagePackObject] class with two [Key(0)] properties and expects an Error-severity MsgPack diagnostic (or AD0001). On head no diagnostic is produced. The same applies to the string-key path at TypeCollector.cs:1039 and the second collector at lines 1163 and 1179.
